newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids flat in light pre-holiday activity.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids flat in light pre-holiday activity.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished flat Wednesday against Tuesday's levels in light pre-holiday activity.
"Demand has not come in. There was not much going on this week," an East Coast physical trader said.
Despite much lower natural gas prices, spot resid prices remained stable in anticipation of end-user demand rising after the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
NYMEX January 1997 Henry Hub natgas futures ended down 8.4 cents at $3.497 per million British thermal units on forecast of lower industrial load and mild weather in the Midwest.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was flat at $22.25-50 a barrel, with December paper at $22.15-$22.35, a tad higher than Tuesday's $22.20-40 range, traders said.
NYH January one percent paper was at $22.25-$22.50, a little softer than $22.40-65 Tuesday.
High sulphurs in NYH also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent still talked on either side of $20.50.
U.S. Gulf prices were stable, with one percent still at $19.50 and three percent at $18.25-50. USG December three percent paper also was discussed at $18.30-45, compared with steady at $18.35-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas was valued Wednesday in the the $4.30s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was quoted lower at about $4.75-90/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.53/mmBtu equivalent.
A upstate New York utility may seek up to 100,000 barrels of 1.5 percent sulfur resid in a tender next week, market sources said.
NYMEX and most utilities in the Northest will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
